decision.reason: One consumer has an executed pass-fail-pass intervention, three consumers have bounded no-repair pass evidence, and all four pass both arms of a source-code-changing compatible release. Independent semantic review and three isolated repetitions remain required.

a1.failure_signature: SLF4J 2 ignores the 1.2.11 binding, falls back to NOPLoggerFactory, and JadlerMockerTest cannot cast it to LoggerContext.

repair_evidence.boundary: The maintainer pull request used SLF4J 2.0.3 and also changed Logback. The intervention keeps SLF4J at 2.0.0 and extracts only the stated Logback compatibility repair.

bounded_negative_consumers.label_boundary: The suite executes PropertyReader and AlgorithmFinder paths that call SLF4J, but neither arm has a logging provider. This is only a no-provider, native-command negative.

bounded_negative_consumers.coverage: The suite executes FreshMarkStepTest and SortPomTest, whose production paths use LoggerFactory.
bounded_negative_consumers.label_boundary: Spotless-lib intentionally has no runtime dependency. The result covers compilation and the testlib formatting paths, not arbitrary consumer logging-provider combinations.

bounded_negative_consumers.coverage: The suite instantiates production logger-bearing classes including RMQConnectionFactory and RMQObjectFactory and exercises message producer paths.
bounded_negative_consumers.label_boundary: SLF4J 2 explicitly ignores Logback 1.2.11 and falls back to a no-operation provider. The result only shows that the native unit-test command does not require a consumer repair after logging output is disabled; it does not show provider compatibility or cover broker-backed integration tests.

rejected_consumer.reason: Both Java 11 arms pass 15 tests, but none of those tests enters the two production logging paths. The result is compilation evidence, not a bounded behavioral negative.

selected.source_change: SLF4J 1.7.30 moves substitute-logger repair, event replay, and substitute-factory clearing into a finally-based post-bind cleanup so initialization failure and no-binding paths are cleaned up as well.
selected.boundary: The native suites exercise LoggerFactory initialization and ordinary logging calls, but do not deliberately force the initialization-failure concurrency paths changed by 1.7.30.

rejected.reason: The release changes build and manifest metadata but no slf4j-api Java source, so green consumers would provide too little semantic evidence for A3.

The original three consumers passed both releases, but rabbitmq-jms-client failed its 1.7.14 arm because Logback 1.2.11 requires org.slf4j.event.LoggingEvent and passed with 1.7.15. It is a repair contrast for this consumer, not a four-consumer no-impact control.

environment_notes: Spotless's embedded Gradle ProjectBuilder derived user.home as '?' in an unmapped container user and intermittently failed while writing a dependency cache. Setting the Java user.home to a writable mounted directory made the unchanged A0 command pass all 155 tests.
Spotless also exposed unrelated first-run dependency-cache failures in Palantir and Flexmark tests. Those failures were retained and were not counted as SLF4J outcomes.
PNC Common initially failed during Java 8 build preparation because its formatting plugin requires Java 11; only the Java 11 runs are compatibility observations.
RabbitMQ JMS integration tests require a broker and are not part of the repository's native unit-test command used here.
next_required_steps: Run three isolated repetitions of A0, A1, A2, A3-before, and A3-after for all four accepted consumers.
Independently review the extracted Jadler repair, the three bounded negative-label ceilings, and whether 1.7.29 to 1.7.30 is an adequate compatible source change.
Do not include this project package in precision or stopping claims until both steps are complete.
